papers.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
papers.abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.

papers.title: Orthograph related to mutual (strong) numerical radius orthogonality on operator algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{B} (H)$ and $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{B} (H)$, respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on $\mathcal{B} (H)$ or $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.

papers.title: Operator systems in \'etale groupoid C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We study operator systems arising from positivity domains of \'etale groupoids with compact unit space. Extending Kavruk's enough unitaries principle we show that such operator systems are hyperrigid in the C$^*$-algebra they generate. We focus on operator systems of positivity domains in UHF algebras and, by identifying them with Cantor graph operator systems, we show that they are hyperrigid. Furthermore, we show that in general, such a characterization is not possible when the \'etaleness condition of the underlying groupoid is removed, due to the failure of reduced spectral and compact operator synthesis.

papers.title: Measure Convergence under Weak Domination for Unitarily Invariant Norms on Finite von Neumann Algebras
papers.abstract: The classical Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem (DCT) is a cornerstone in commutative measure theory, while its extension to the noncommutative setting has remained a longstanding challenge due to the barriers posed by the noncommutative structure. Let \(\alpha\) be a unitarily invariant norm defined on a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra \((\mathcal{M}, \tau)\), let $L^\alpha(\mathcal M, \tau)$ be the completion of $\mathcal M$ with respect to the norm $\alpha$(which includes all $L^p(\mathcal M, \tau)$ as special cases). In this paper, by replacing ``almost everywhere convergence" with Nelson's convergence in measure, we establish a noncommutative analog of the dominated convergence theorem for $L^\alpha(\mathcal M, \tau)$ under a { significantly weaker dominating condition} than those previously considered. For instance, in a \(II_1\) factor \(\mathcal{M}\), if \(P\) is a projection with \(\tau(P)=\frac{1}{n}\), then \(n^2 P\) ``dominates" every operator of norm \(\leq n\). As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of center-preserving $*$-automorphism of finite von Neumann algebras, which unifies and extends the earlier works of Kadison and Haagerup on the structure of automorphisms.

papers.title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
papers.abstract: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
papers.abstract: We prove that a weight on a C$^*$-algebra is lower semi-continuous if it is lower semi-continuous on commutative C$^*$-subalgebras. This can be used to prove a von Neumann algebraic counterpart that a weight on a von Neumann algebra is normal if it is normal on commutative von Neumann subalgebras. This provides an affirmative solution to Haagerup's second problem (Problem 1.11) on normal weights posed in 1975.

papers.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
papers.abstract: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $\lambda>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ \alpha=\frac{\lambda(1-2/q)} {12(\lambda t_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.

papers.title: $T$-admissible processes and noncommutative weighted ergodic theorems
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the bilaterally almost uniform (b.a.u.) convergence of weighted averages of a positive Dunford-Schwartz operator $T$ acting on the noncommutative $L_p$-spaces $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ associated to a semifinite von Neumann algebra $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$ for a variety of sequences which includes those generated by bounded i.i.d. sequences, the M\"{o}bius function, the Liouville function, and totally balanced automatic sequences. If $1<p<\infty$, then sequences generated by i.i.d. sequences with finite $q$-th moment for $q=\frac{p}{p-1}$ being the H\"{o}lder conjugate of $p$ are also shown to generate good weights for $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We also study similar problems for $T$-admissible processes on a semifinite von Neumann algebra, showing that if a Wiener-Wintner type ergodic theorem holds for a class $\mathcal{W}\subset W_q$ of weights, then it also holds for strongly $p$-bounded $T$-admissible processes assuming that the duality $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$ holds and that $T$ is a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism. A version of this result for arbitrary positive Dunford-Schwartz operators is also considered.

papers.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

papers.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.

papers.title: Word Trace Formulas over Compact Groups and Connected Cumulants
papers.abstract: We compute the expected value of the product of traces for a finite set of words within any compact subgroup of $\mathcal(N)$. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition under which these values determine that the product of the conjugacy classes of the words contains the identity.

papers.title: How characterisations of traces and central elements fail: sharp violation constants via michelson contrast and noncentrality
papers.abstract: A positive functional is a trace if and only if it satisfies any one of many inequalities, the first being Gardner's $|\varphi(X)|\le\varphi(|X|)$; positive central elements are characterised similarly. We ask how strongly these characterisations fail. For $\varphi=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,\cdot)$ on a matrix algebra the natural scale is the Michelson contrast $\delta$ of the density. For Gardner's inequality the sharp constant depends on $\delta$ and on the contrast $\delta'$ of $|X|$ only through their product: it is $(1-\delta^2\delta'^2)^{-1/2}$, the secant of the angle whose sine is $\delta\delta'$. On a finite von Neumann algebra the contrast is the wrong parameter, since every central density gives a trace; the governing parameter is the noncentrality, defined through the central condition number $\kappa_Z(\rho)$ of the central envelopes of $\rho$ (the largest and smallest elements of Halpern's central spectrum). A transfer principle lifts sharp matrix constants to exact constants in terms of $\kappa_Z$ in every finite von Neumann algebra. For 38 trace characterisations the constant is exact in 23 cases, has proved bounds in 13 and is known only numerically in two; for instance it is $\cosh(\frac12\ln\kappa_Z)$ for Gardner's inequality and for the subadditivity of the modulus. On matrix algebras the finite exact violations vanish at the trace to the orders $\delta$, $\delta^2$ or $\delta^4$, and outside factors and abelian algebras no function of the contrast describes the constants. We also find the sharp constants of the Novikov-Tikhonov characterisations of central elements, sharp bounds for three unnormalised trace functionals, and sharp contrast thresholds below which subadditivity of the square root and the power-mean inequality cannot fail. A numerical search, certified as a lower bound for each supremum, supports conjectured values for the remaining inequalities.

papers.title: Local Reflexivity and Exactness for Reduced $C^*$-Algebras of Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every countable non-exact discrete group $H$ and every nontrivial countable discrete group $K$, the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is not locally reflexive. These provide the first known examples of non-locally reflexive reduced group $C^*$-algebras, settling a longstanding existence question. Moreover, for every nontrivial countable exact discrete group $K$, we establish that local reflexivity of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is equivalent to exactness of $H$, and hence to exactness of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$. This gives a partial affirmative answer to Kirchberg's question of whether local reflexivity implies exactness for $C^*$-algebras. As applications, we construct finitely generated groups with the Haagerup property, as well as finitely generated residually finite groups, whose reduced group $C^*$-algebras are not locally reflexive. In particular, neither the Haagerup property nor coarse embeddability into Hilbert space guarantees local reflexivity of the associated reduced group $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
papers.abstract: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.

papers.title: $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless inclusions for the infinite braid group
papers.abstract: Let $B_\infty$ be the braid group on infinitely many strands and $P_\infty$ its pure braid group. We show that $C^*_r(P_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ and all its intermediate inclusions are $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and completely selfless. This gives natural examples of simple nonnuclear $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $C^*$-algebras. Further examples come from $\mathrm{SL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$. We also show that $C^*_r(\mathbb{F}_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ is completely selfless for the free group $\mathbb{F}_\infty$ of braids in which only the first strand moves. All results hold for twisted group $C^*$-algebras. In contrast, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability fails for $B_n$ with $n$ finite and for groups that are not inner amenable.

papers.title: Intermediate subalgebras of cross-product von Neumann algebras arising from weakly compact actions
papers.abstract: In this short paper, we establish the following Galois-type property for all measure-preserving, weakly compact actions $G \curvearrowright (X,\mu) $ of a non-inner amenable group $G$ on a standard probability space $X$: for any intermediate von Neumann subalgebra $\mathcal L(G)\subseteq \mathcal N \subseteq L^\infty (X)\rtimes G$, there is a factor $G\curvearrowright Y$ of $G \curvearrowright X$ such that $\mathcal N= L^\infty(Y)\rtimes G$. In particular, this holds for all pmp distal actions $G\curvearrowright X$, thereby answering positively an open problem from \cite{BCCMSW24} (which can also be traced back to \cite{CD20}). We also provide an example showing our result is optimal.

papers.title: Sharp Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Semigroups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp $2$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroups with $-1<q<1$ and obtain hypercontractivity along the Gross curve with the optimal coefficient, and determine the exact hypercontractive time for $1<p\le2\le r<\infty$. Reverse hypercontractivity holds in the two separate ranges $0<p<r<1$ and $-\infty<p<r<0$. An explicit counterexample rules out the proposed universal reverse curve across zero. We also obtain the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality via the intertwining property.

papers.title: Weakly Unitary Zeon Matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, zeon matrix groups are discussed for the first time. Extending the concept of unitary complex matrices (i.e., matrices $A$ such that $A^\dagger A=\mI$) to matrices having entries in the complex zeon algebra $\CZ$, a ``zeon dagger'' operator $\zdag$ is defined and used to declare a zeon matrix $\Xi$ to be {\em unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI$. The unitary zeon matrices of order $n$ form a subgroup $\U_n$ of all invertible order-$n$ zeon matrices. A more interesting notion is that of ``weak unitarity'' of a zeon matrix. In particular, a zeon matrix $\Xi$ will be said to be {\em weakly unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI+\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a diagonal nilpotent zeon matrix. The weakly unitary matrices of order $n$ form a group $\W_n$, of which $\U_n$ is a subgroup. It is further shown that the exponential of a graph's nilpotent adjacency matrix has a natural orthogonal decomposition into the sum of a weakly unitary zeon matrix and a nilpotent zeon matrix. Eigenvalues of the weakly unitary zeon matrix reveal information about the graph's cycles and paths.

papers.title: Regularity and selfless cp maps
papers.abstract: We investigate the regularity properties of C*-algebras admitting a weakly selfless unital completely positive map.

papers.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $\sigma$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,\sigma)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action $\alpha$ satisfies that $\overline{\alpha(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,\sigma)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $\alpha$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $\alpha:G\curvearrowright (D,\sigma)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action with $\overline{\alpha(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

papers.title: Skew fields of non-commutative meromorphic functions affiliated to finite operator algebras
papers.abstract: We embed skew fields of meromorphic functions in several non-commuting variables into the topological $*-$algebra of closed linear operators affiliated to a finite von Neumann algebra, $\mathfrak{M}$, with faithful, normal tracial state, $\tau$. Namely, let $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$, $r \in (0, +\infty]$, denote the rings of formal power series in $d \in \mathbb{N}$ non-commuting variables with "radius of convergence" at least $r$ and let $\Xi \in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$ be a tuple of row-norm $<r$ with the property that there exist no non-zero trace-class operators $T_1, \cdots, T_d \in \mathscr{B} (L^2 (\mathfrak{M}, \tau))$ obeying $\sum _j [T_j , \Xi _j] =0$. Then the unital homomorphism $\mathscr{O} _d (r) \rightarrow \mathfrak{M}$ defined by the evaluation, $\mathfrak{z} _j \mapsto \Xi _j$, extends to an embedding of the universal skew field of fractions of $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$ into the $*-$algebra of closed operators affiliated to $\mathfrak{M}$. In their $L^2-$homology theory of von Neumann algebras, Connes and Shlyakhtenko defined a certain quantity, $0 \leq \Delta (\Xi) \leq d$, as the Murray-von Neumann co-dimension of the Hilbert module generated by all $d-$tuples of finite rank operators obeying the above commutator condition with $\Xi \in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$. As demonstrated by Mai, Speicher and Yin, this $\Delta$ measures, in a certain precise sense, the algebraic independence of the components of $\Xi$. Connes-Shlyakhtenko proved that $\Delta$ is an upper bound for Voiculescu's non-microstates free entropy dimension, $\delta ^* (\Xi)$, and remark that it is of interest to determine whether these two quantities are equal. Using non-commutative function theory, we show that this is generally not the case, by constructing a triple of self-adjoint operators, $\Xi = (\Xi_1,\Xi_2,\Xi_3)$, for which this inequality is strict, $\delta^*(\Xi) < \Delta(\Xi)$.

papers.title: A Reduction Bound for Entanglement Detection by Positive Free Maps
papers.abstract: Collins, Hayden, and Nechita used free probability to construct families of $k$-positive but not $(k+1)$-positive maps and applied them to entanglement detection. We prove that positive free maps associated with compactly supported freely infinitely divisible distributions are no stronger than the reduction criterion in every ancillary dimension. In particular, these maps cannot detect positive partial transpose entanglement. The proof combines a joint Fock realization with an operator positivity certificate derived from free L\'evy data.

papers.title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.

papers.title: Fej\'er--Riesz factorization for positive noncommutative trigonometric polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a Fej\'er-Riesz type factorization for positive matrix-valued noncommutative trigonometric polynomials on $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, where $\mathscr{W}$ is either the free semigroup $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{g}$, and $\mathfrak{Y}$ is a discrete group. More precisely, using the shortlex order, if $A$ has degree at most $w$ in the $\mathscr{W}$ variables and is uniformly strictly positive on all unitary representations of $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, then $A=B^{*}B$ with $B$ analytic and of $\mathscr{W}$-degree at most $w$; this degree bound is optimal, and strict positivity is essential. As an application, we obtain degree-bounded sums-of-squares certificates for Bell-type inequalities in $\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}\times \mathbb{Z}_2^{*h}]$ from quantum information theory. In the special case $\mathscr{W}=\mathbb{Z}^h$ we recover, in the matrix-valued setting, the classical commutative multivariable Fej\'er-Riesz factorization. For trivial $\mathfrak{Y}$ we obtain a ``perfect'' group-algebra Positivstellensatz on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ that does not require strict positivity; this result is sharp, as demonstrated by counterexamples in $\mathbb{Z}_2*\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3^{*2}$. To establish our main results two novel ingredients of independent interest are developed: (a) a positive-semidefinite Parrott theorem with entries given by functions on a group; and (b) solutions to positive semidefinite matrix completion problems for $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ indexed by words in $\mathscr{W}$ of length $\le w$.

papers.title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\lambda P_\lambda$, where $\Lambda\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}P_\lambda=I$ in the strong operator topology. We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$. We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.

papers.title: Teleportation=Translation: Continuous recovery of black hole information
papers.abstract: The \textit{Teleportation=Translation} conjecture posits that the recovery of information from a black hole is dual to a geometric translation in the emergent spacetime. In this paper, we establish this equivalence for general local quantum field theories by constructing a continuous unitary interpolation that bridges discrete algebraic teleportation protocols and continuous modular flow. We resolve the failure of dynamic idempotency, fundamentally inherent in Type III von Neumann algebras, by employing the Haagerup-Kosaki crossed-product construction. This lift to the semifinite Type~II$_\infty$ envelope yields a canonical, dynamically consistent path. Crucially, we prove that its unique infinitesimal generator $\tilde{G}$ is exactly twice the geometric modular momentum ($\tilde{G}=2P$). We establish this identity as a closed operator equivalence using Nelson's analytic vector theorem and quantify its structural robustness via non-commutative $L^p$ theory. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unitary information recovery fundamentally manifests as a continuous geometric translation. This provides a rigorous operator-algebraic mechanism for resolving the black hole information paradox, offering a kinematic framework naturally extendable to include gravitational back-reaction.

papers.title: Spectral gap, internality of relative commutants, and non-hyperlinear groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the relative commutant of a finite unitary tuple in a tracial matrix ultraproduct is internal whenever its conjugation operator has a spectral gap off the commutant. This implies the existence of a non-hyperlinear group.

papers.title: $\mathcal{W}$-absorbing actions of finite groups on the Razak-Jacelon algebra
papers.abstract: We say that a countable discrete group action $\alpha$ on a C$^*$-algebra $A$ is \textit{$\mathcal{W}$-absorbing} if there exist a C$^*$-algebra $B$ and an action $\beta$ on $B$ such that $\alpha$ is cocycle conjugate to $\beta\otimes \mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{W}}$ on $B\otimes \mathcal{W}$ where $\mathcal{W}$ is the Razak-Jacelon algebra. In this paper, we completely classify outer $\mathcal{W}$-absorbing actions of finite groups on $\mathcal{W}$ up to conjugacy and cocycle conjugacy.

papers.title: Functional Calculus on Noncommutative Tori, II. Complex Powers, Logarithms, and Sectorial Projections
papers.abstract: This paper develops a systematic theory of complex powers, logarithms, and sectorial projections of elliptic pseudodifferential operators on noncommutative tori, extending to this setting the classical constructions of Seeley and others. Building on the parametric pseudodifferential calculus of the prequel~\cite{LP:Part1}, we construct the complex powers associated with a given ray, show that they form a holomorphic family of pseudodifferential operators with the semigroup property, and compute their symbols. We further establish exponential growth bounds on vertical strips in the operator, Schatten, and trace-class topologies by means of a new holomorphic calculus for pseudodifferential families. The logarithm is identified as a pseudodifferential operator whose symbol is determined by the resolvent symbol, and the associated trace formula is derived. Sectorial projections are constructed as contour integrals and shown to be of order zero. This yields analogues for noncommutative tori of results of Wodzicki, Okikiolu, and Gaarde--Grubb, and provides the analytic foundations for the spectral-geometric applications developed in subsequent papers.

papers.title: Maximal Algebraic Ideals in Nonunital $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of maximal algebraic two-sided ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras. We formulate singular-distribution estimates in terms of lower semicontinuous $2$-quasitraces and introduce a novel criterion, which we call an admissible compact quasitracial triple set. These tools allow us to control membership in algebraic ideals and to prove the nonexistence of maximal ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras under a closed finite-scale face condition. This nonexistence result applies to a broad class of simple $C^*$-algebras including simple separable stable AF algebras, and nonunital, simple, separable, stably finite, $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras $A$ that admit an approximate identity consisting of increasing projections $(p_n)$ and for which the simplex $\operatorname{QT}_2^1(A,p_1)$ of normalized traces at $p_1$ has finitely many extreme points. Moreover, we construct a simple AF algebra whose finite-scale face is dense but not closed and which nevertheless has a maximal dense algebraic ideal. This example yields a negative resolution to a question raised by Ozawa, asking whether every maximal algebraic two-sided ideal in a $C^*$-algebra must be closed.
